title: Directional Flow and Mirrored Corner Panels
description: Introduce an explicit directional-flow system for the UI library (ui/js/react/index.tsx): every element gets a horizontal flow (ltr|rtl) and vertical flow (down|up), default LTR+down with icons at the trailing edge (label-then-icon, flipping today's icon-first order globally for Button/Toggle/Action/tab buttons). Tree rows keep icon at flow-start. Mechanism: a FlowProvider React context (cloned from the LevelProvider pattern) that CornerPanel sets from its corner via flowFromCorner(); horizontal mirroring rides on native CSS `dir="rtl"` on the corner-panel root so flex/grid auto-mirror (Tailwind v4's divide-x already emits logical border-inline-*, and built-in logical utilities like text-start/ms-auto exist). Right corners (top-right, bottom-right) become full horizontal mirrors: icon left of label, right-aligned text, tree gutter/chevron/guides on the right, scrollbar on the left. Bottom corners keep only their existing chrome+tab-row vertical mirror (tree content stays top-to-bottom). Work includes: ui.css logical utility additions (ms-*/me-*/ps-*/pe-* alongside existing ml-*/mr-*/pl-*/pr-*), FlowProvider/useFlow/flowFromCorner region, icon-trailing flips at ButtonGroupItem/ToggleGroupItem/ActionGroupItem/Action/PanelTabRow, dir wiring on CornerPanel + portalled overlay content (Popover/Select/Tooltip/Dialog/ContextMenu), physical-to-logical class conversions at enumerated flow-relative sites (tree gutter/guides, labels, navbar toggle, command shortcut, kbd, dropdown check icon, detail-panel, toggle-strip separator) while windows/mode-dock/canvas stay physical, dock drag-and-drop insert-index math inversion for RTL rows in computeTabDockDropZone, test updates/additions, and periphery (ui-interpreter.tsx value row, Storybook Panel stories). Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/ui-the-design-language-quirky-sifakis.md.
summary:
Fixed the navbar's corner panels reflowing navbar content instead of floating over it, like the footer's do.

Root cause: `framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx` computed `navbarStyle` — `{paddingLeft, paddingRight}` derived from the top-left/top-right corner panel's `visible`/`size` state — and passed it as literal `style` on `<Navbar>`, which applied it directly to the `<nav>` element. That's real CSS padding, not an overlay: opening a top corner panel shrank the navbar's own content box, visually pushing/reflowing its items (title, breadcrumbs, fullscreen toggle) instead of letting the panel sit on top of an untouched navbar — the opposite of the corner-panel design intent, and inconsistent with `Footer`, which never had any such mechanism (`<Footer items={[]} />`, no dynamic style, plain `inset-0` centered-item overlay).

Fix:
- `os-shell.tsx`: removed `topLeftPanel`/`topRightPanel`/`navbarStyle` entirely; `<Navbar>` is now invoked plainly (`<Navbar items={navbarItems} showFullscreenToggle />`), matching how `<Footer>` is invoked.
- `ui/js/react/index.tsx`: removed the now-dead `style` prop from `NavbarProps`/`Navbar` (confirmed via repo-wide grep it was the only consumer — no coda/compose/Storybook usage), and simplified the centered-items overlay from `absolute inset-y-0 left-0 right-0` + a dynamic `style={{left, right}}` inset to a plain `absolute inset-0`, identical to `Footer`'s.

Verified: full `ui-react` vitest suite passes with the same stable 14 pre-existing/unrelated failures as before this fix (11 known baseline + 3 traced earlier to a concurrent developer's in-progress Tree/Layout refactor on this same file) — no regressions. Could not get a fresh live screenshot this round: the note-react-dev preview port was being held by a different concurrent Claude Code session in this same folder (confirmed via the harness's own "another chat's dev server is running in this folder" notice, and `preview_start`/`preview_list` returning no live process from this session despite repeated attempts) — this is an environment/session contention issue, not related to the fix itself. Confidence in the fix is based on: (a) precisely identifying the exact CSS mechanism causing the reported symptom, (b) the fix being a direct structural match to Footer's already-correct, already-verified-live behavior, and (c) the full test suite passing clean.
